extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians specializing in inter-universal Teichmüller theory / arithmetic geometry (readers of IUTch I–III)
extracted.subtask_description: Precise definitions and functorial group-theoretic algorithms for constructing split theta monoids, constant monoids, Gaussian (gau) monoids, and their properties (multiradiality/uniradiality, conjugate synchronisation, splittings up to torsion) in the IUT framework; includes local (v-adic) versions and evaluation morphisms. Targets the formal reconstruction and compatibilities used across IUTch II/III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Split Theta Monoids (M-theoretic)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Definition 11.12 (1)) Collections of submonoids O2(M(…)) (and related objects) functorially group-theoretically reconstructed as submonoids of H^1(...), equipped with natural conjugation actions of the relevant tempered/topological group; each such reconstructed object is referred to as a mono-theta-theoretic theta monoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are defined via the constructions of IUTchII Proposition 3.1 and are given together with splittings up to torsion determined by Corollary 11.11. The phrasing emphasises functorial reconstruction and the presence of conjugation actions; treat the reconstructed monoids and their splittings up to torsion as the canonical outputs of the algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant Monoids (M-theoretic)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Definition 11.12 (2)) Using the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism via positive rational structure and local class field theory (LCFT) and the surjection H^1(G_v; Z_hat) → Z_hat, one takes inverse images to obtain functorial group-theoretic reconstructions of constant monoids (mono-theta-theoretic constant monoid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction depends on the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism via positive rational structure and LCFT and uses value-group data; the resulting constant monoids carry natural conjugation actions and are reconstructed up to inner automorphism/indeterminacy. This construction is noted to be uniradially defined in places where the value-group is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: (Definition 11.13 (1)) From a tempered Frobenioid and a choice of Frobenioid-theoretic theta function one obtains submonoids (on D_v) and collections of conjugate submonoids with natural (π_1/Aut)-actions; these are called Frobenioid-theoretic theta monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The choice of theta-function-datum determines monoids O_3(...) on D_v and the various conjugates yield collections of submonoids; splittings up to torsion exist and the reconstructions are well-defined up to inner automorphism. Compatibility with the (cid:5)_v-action and with splittings up to torsion is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenioid-theoretic constant monoid
rubrics_metrics.description: (Definition 11.13 (2)) From the pre-Frobenioid structure on C_v one obtains a monoid O_3(C_v) on D_v (called (cid:9)_{Cv}), equipped with the natural (cid:5)_v-action; this is reconstructible from the Frobenioid up to inner automorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises that the constant monoid is an output of the Frobenioid data and is determined only up to inner automorphism arising from the (cid:5)_v; the object is used as the constant-container for theta-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections of Kummer isomorphisms (F-theoretic)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Proposition 11.14 (1)) For suitable objects S with abstract cyclotomic/exterior cyclotome structure, one obtains collections of Kummer isomorphisms of monoids, well-defined up to inner automorphism and compatible with conjugation actions and splittings up to torsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Kummer isomorphism-collections are constructed via Kummer theory and are required to be compatible with the respective conjugation action of the tempered group and with monoid splittings up to torsion, under suitable bijections of ℓ-adic torsors. The usual indeterminacy is inner automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradiality of Split Theta Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: (Proposition 11.15 (1)) Under a full poly-isomorphism of projective systems of mono-theta environments, the constructions/algorithms that produce split theta monoids (and associated data) are multiradially defined: isomorphisms induce compatible collections of isomorphisms and the functorial algorithm is multiradial in the sense of the natural functor Graph of Proposition 11.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiradiality here means the algorithm is compatible with arbitrary automorphisms of the relevant pairs (G_v(...), (1)(cid:9)yF...), up to specified torsion indeterminacies; manifests as compatibility diagrams and collections of isomorphisms. This property is a desired behaviour for the theta-level constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniradiality of Constant Monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: (Proposition 11.15 (2)) The algorithms constructing constant monoids (especially those using cyclotomic rigidity via positive rational structure and LCFT and the H^1 surjection) are only uniradially defined: isomorphisms induce collections of isomorphisms but the functorial algorithm fails to be compatible with certain automorphisms of the pairs, hence is uniradial rather than multiradial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry highlights that constant-monoid constructions use additional value-group data and LCFT; consequences include incompatibility with some automorphisms (an important limitation/anti-pattern). One must track uniradiality when using constant monoids in later arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate Synchronisation (Gaussian/M-theoretic)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Corollary 11.16 (1) and repeated) By regarding cuspidal inertia subgroups labelled by t as subgroups of cuspidal inertia of the ambient tempered object, one obtains Fo_6-symmetrising isomorphisms ('conjugate synchronisation') which induce isomorphisms between labelled pairs (G_v(...), constant_monoid(...)) for distinct labels t; these permit construction of diagonal/symmetrised objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjugate synchronisation produces labelled isomorphisms compatible with Fo_6-symmetrising maps; the diagonal (symmetrised) objects and associated restriction maps are well-defined up to inner automorphism (and inner automorphism indeterminacy is independent of the label). Use of these synchronisations is required to build Gaussian/value-profile constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gaussian Monoids (mono-theta-theoretic)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Corollary 11.16 (2)) From a value-profile (an element of a certain product of constant-monoid copies) one obtains two collections of submonoids (denoted (cid:9)gau and 1(cid:9)gau), called mono-theta-theoretic Gaussian monoids; these objects are equipped with natural G_v-actions, splittings up to torsion, and come with evaluation isomorphisms induced by restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Gaussian monoids are constructed functorially from M(...) using Fo_6-symmetrising isomorphisms and Corollary 11.11. The construction yields value-profiles of cardinality (2^l)^l and evaluation maps (env -> gau) well-defined up to inner automorphism; splittings up to torsion and compatibility with G_v-actions are required properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant Monoids and Splittings (Gaussian context)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Corollary 11.16 (3)) The diagonal-in-labels submonoid of the constant monoids determines an isomorphism between a 'zero-labelled' diagonal submonoid and the diagonal-in-F^l submonoid, giving a graph of monoids and splittings up to torsion compatible with labelled G_v-actions and restriction isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a canonical splitting (up to torsion) used to compare Gaussian monoids' diagonal fibre with the constant monoid; required compatibility with restriction maps and with the earlier Definition 11.12(1) splittings is emphasised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniradiality of Gaussian analogues (theta-values level)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Remark 11.17.2) A Gaussian analogue of Proposition 11.15 at the theta-values (gau) level is only uniradially defined, because construction of constant monoids (used as containers of theta values) relies on cyclotomic rigidity via positive rational structure and LCFT; theta-function/envelope level (env-labelled) constructions can be multiradial but gau-level ones are not without further modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This points out a structural limitation/anti-pattern: to make the Gaussian (gau) algorithms multiradial one must admit mild indeterminacies (Indet *, Indet !, Indet xy) or later use log-shells as in Theorem 13.12. Users should track where uniradiality enters and where later corrections are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local (v-adic) Constant Monoids and functorial reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: (Proposition 11.18 (1)) For v in V_good (or appropriate local sets), there is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm reconstructing ind-topological submonoids equipped with G_v-actions (or topological monoids from split monoids D'_v) via inverse limits H^1(J; Z_hat) over open subgroups J. These outputs are isomorphic to (G_v × O_3 F_v)-type objects and are canonical up to inner automorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the local analogue of global constant-monoid constructions used to build theta/gau objects at places v. The algorithmic reconstruction is explicit: form lim_{open J} H^1(J; Z_hat) etc. Note again the presence of inner-automorphism indeterminacy and the dependence on the topological/split monoid input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic Semi-simplifications (local)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Proposition 11.18 (2)) From the local topological group G_v (or split monoid D'_v) one constructs a topological monoid with a distinguished formal element log_{G_v}(p_v) in R^0(G_v) and a natural isomorphism from the semisimplified constant monoid ((cid:9)cns(...)/(cid:2))-R to an R'-module (R'_{(cid:21)0})_v; define (cid:9)ss_cns(...) as the semisimplified version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplies a semisimplified/mono-analytic version of the constant monoid adapted to R^0-modules and introduces the formal log-symbols used in later evaluation. The construction is functorial and the distinguished log element is required for theta/gau evaluation maps at v.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta and Gaussian Monoids at good places and formal evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: (Proposition 11.18 (4)) Locally at v one defines (cid:9)env((cid:5)_v) (theta monoid), (cid:9)gau((cid:5)_v) (Gaussian monoid) and formal evaluation eval: env -> gau sending formal log symbols to tuples of formal logs; this evaluation restricts to identity on copies of the semisimplified constant monoid and is compatible with G_v-actions and splittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires holomorphic structures for labels and Fo_6-synchronising isomorphisms in some variants; the evaluation map is a formal algebraic construction used to pass from theta-type data to gau-type/value-profile data at each place, and must preserve the constant-part and be compatible with group actions and splittings up to torsion.
